risks.title: Dependence on USA-Mexico passenger traffic
risks.summary: ASRMF is highly dependent on the USA-Mexico corridor for its airport revenues. Trump-era trade tariffs, migration restrictions, and U.S. border policies directly threaten international passenger traffic to Cancún, Cozumel, and the Riviera Maya, which account for over 60% of international traffic at Mexican airports.
risks.score_rationale: Major risk positioned early in Item 1A with highly intensive language (repeated use of « material adverse effect »). 61-62% of Mexico's international traffic comes from the U.S.; 51-52% of Mexican passenger revenues depend on international passengers. Trend is stable but structural vulnerability to U.S. trade and migration policies remains high.

risks.title: Political and economic instability Mexico-USA-Colombia
risks.summary: Changes in trade and migration policies under the Trump administration (tariffs, USMCA, mass deportations) create major uncertainty about economic conditions in Mexico and Colombia. ASRMF cannot control these geopolitical factors, which directly affect travel demand and tourism decisions to its destinations.
risks.score_rationale: Major geopolitical risk with highly alarming language (« material adverse effect », « cannot assure »). Mentioned early in Item 1A with details on Trump administration changes, USMCA, and reciprocal tariffs. Trend clearly rising with new measures expected in 2025-2026. Very high categorical weight for a regional airport operator.

risks.title: Health crises and pandemics affecting air traffic
risks.summary: Epidemics and pandemics (COVID-19, H1N1, avian flu) drastically reduce passenger traffic and increase aviation security costs. ASRMF has already experienced the impact of COVID-19 and remains vulnerable to future global health crises affecting travel demand.
risks.score_rationale: Systemic risk mentioned multiple times in Item 1A with references to COVID-19, H1N1, and avian flu. Language is moderate but clear on past (COVID-19) and potential future impact. Trend is stable but residual risk remains high post-pandemic. Applicable to all ASRMF airports.

risks.title: Natural disasters (hurricanes, earthquakes)
risks.summary: Seasonal hurricanes (Q3) and earthquakes threaten airport infrastructure and reduce tourist traffic to Cancún, Cozumel, Riviera Maya, and Puerto Rico. ASRMF only insures physical damage, not business interruption; climate change may increase the frequency of such events.
risks.score_rationale: Operational risk specific to ASRMF's geography (southeast Mexico, Colombia, Puerto Rico). Intensive language with concrete examples (Hurricanes Irma, Maria, Fiona 2022; Puerto Rico earthquakes 2019-2020). Trend is stable but experts note increasing frequency and severity due to climate change. Insurance coverage is limited (no business interruption protection).

risks.title: Internal armed conflicts in Colombia (ELN, FARC)
risks.summary: Internal armed conflicts in Colombia (ELN, FARC) have recently intensified, particularly in the El Catatumbo region. ASRMF's El Caraño airport has been affected by these conflicts in the past; the current escalation creates uncertainty around future Colombian operations.
risks.score_rationale: Regional risk specific to Colombian operations. Language is measured (« cannot predict ») but acknowledges recent escalation in El Catatumbo and past impact on El Caraño airport. Trend is rising (« recently escalated »). Moderate weight as impact is limited to Colombian operations, not the core Mexican business.

risks.title: Prolonged economic crisis in Puerto Rico (PROMESA, PREPA)
risks.summary: Puerto Rico has been experiencing a prolonged economic crisis since 2006, worsened by hurricanes, COVID-19, and debt restructuring (PROMESA). LMM Airport (60% ASRMF) is affected by this recession; electricity rates are expected to rise and PREPA restructuring remains uncertain (fifth adjustment plan ongoing).
risks.score_rationale: Risk specific to LMM Airport (60% ASRMF joint venture). Detailed language on recession since 2006, PROMESA debt restructuring, and ongoing PREPA adjustment plan (fifth amendment in March 2025). Trend is stable but uncertainty remains high regarding PREPA restructuring and electricity rate increases. Moderate weight as LMM is a minority part of the portfolio.

risks.title: Geopolitical escalation in the Middle East (Iran, Israel, USA)
risks.summary: Geopolitical escalation in the Middle East (Israel-Hamas-Iran conflict, US-Israel strikes in February 2026, Iranian retaliation in April 2026) creates major volatility in energy markets and trade routes. This reduces demand for air travel and increases security costs, directly affecting ASRMF's passenger revenues.
risks.score_rationale: Emerging major risk described in detail (Hamas attack October 7, 2023, US-Israel strikes February 28, 2026, Iranian retaliation April 2026). Language is highly alarming (« highly unpredictable », « material adverse effect », « sustained volatility »). Trend is clearly rising with ongoing escalation. Impact on energy markets, trade routes, and travel demand.

risks.title: Dependence on passenger revenues (41-46% of total)
risks.summary: ASRMF's revenues are highly dependent on passenger charges (41-46% of total). Any shock reducing passenger traffic (recession, pandemic, terrorism, natural disaster, migration restrictions) directly impacts operational profitability and debt servicing capacity.
risks.score_rationale: Core business risk: 41.3% of 2025 revenues came from passenger charges (vs 46.1% in 2024). Language clearly highlights structural dependence. Trend is stable but vulnerability to any traffic-affecting shock (economic, health, security) remains high. Very high categorical weight for an airport operator.
